_doc: CF-UNPARSED-IS-NOT-UNNUMBERED census. READ-ONLY measurement of the sold_comps rows whose cardNumber segment is the `player-<name>` pseudo-number. Produced by scripts/census-player-pseudo-number.cjs against prod on 2026-09-04, post-#1715. Nothing was written.

_verdicts.reparse: the row's own title states a real card number -- the row was never unnumbered, it was UNPARSED. A re-derivation gives it a numbered identity, and the rematch classifier treats that as IMPROVE when the numbered identity is checklist-backed.
_verdicts.unnumbered: the card genuinely carries no number: the row's fields assert it (`nno`/`unnumbered`) or the product is one of the families that never had numbers (T206, Magic Alpha/Beta, Signature Series, Stand-Ups, Rub-Offs). The pseudo-number is the right answer and the row stays where it is.
_verdicts.underivable: no number to read and nothing asserting there is none. Absent beats wrong: reported, never keyed.

_headline: Only 1.6% of the 89,197-row population is the one CF-PLAYER-IS-THE-NUMBER was written for. 26.4% have a card number stated in their own title that the deriver threw away, and 72.0% have no identity to derive at all.
_readingTheTop20: `setKey: unknown` dominates the head and is almost entirely UNDERIVABLE. Those rows are missing a PRODUCT as well as a number, so the pseudo-number was never the only thing wrong with them -- they need the setKey acquisition lane, not this one.

The genuinely productive lane is the NAMED products: 2026 topps (977 of 1,327 reparse), 2025 topps (589 of 1,211), 2025 mp (394 of 685). A modern flagship card always has a number, so a `player-` row on one is the defect by definition.

1997 japanese-rocket-gang is the only row in the top 20 with a real `unnumbered` count (237). Japanese Pokemon promos genuinely ship without collector numbers, which is the population the pseudo-number exists for -- and 445 of the same product's rows DO state a number, so the product needs both answers, not one.

_whatTheSamplesShow: The UNDERIVABLE samples show a SECOND defect riding along: the player field itself is corrupted. `player-kawhi-leonard-tie-dye` swallowed the parallel, `player-mega-box-elly-de` swallowed the product and truncated the name, `player-pokemon-swsh-fa-mew` is not a person at all. A pseudo-number built out of a bad player parse is a slug that names nothing -- another reason the shape must not be reachable from a parse failure.

The REPARSE samples name the hazard the classifier must survive: a multi-card lot title ('#31 Ron Brewer Fred Brown', 'DeBusschere #10 Bob Lanier #11') states a number that may belong to a DIFFERENT card. The existing lot guard (parserSaysLot + the card-number-range vocabulary) and the checklist-backed gate both stand between that title and a write; this census sizes the lane, it does not authorize it.
_scope: REPORT ONLY. No row was re-keyed by this census, and the classifier change it accompanies makes `player-` -> numbered eligible for IMPROVE only when the title states the number AND the numbered identity is checklist-backed AND the provenance tier is AUTO. Every other row stays exactly where it is.
